title: Workflows, agents and who controls the steps

items.stem: Two designs for the makerspace assistant answer the same student question, "Can I use the laser cutter Friday?". Design A: the program always calls search_manuals, then check_calendar, then makes one model call to write the reply. Design B: the program gives the model the same two tools plus a goal, and the model decides which tool to use, in what order, and when to stop. Label each design as a workflow or an agent, and state the one criterion that separates them (one or two sentences).

A Python script handles each student message by making three model calls, one after another, in this order every time: (1) classify the message as a booking request or a manual question, (2) extract the machine name and date, (3) draft a reply from those results. A teammate asks how to label this design. Which label and reason is correct?

options.text: An agent, because the model is called several times and each call builds on the output of the one before
An agent, because the model decides what text to write at each of the three steps
An agent, because one step has the model work out which machine and date the student means
A workflow, because the code fixes the order of the steps and the model only supplies each step's content
A workflow, because it makes exactly three model calls, and an agent has to make more than three
A workflow, because it has no loop, and any design that contains a loop is automatically an agent

items.stem: Every booking request in the makerspace assistant must go through the same three actions in the same order: check the calendar for the slot, check the student's training record, then create the booking. Your sponsor gave you a small model budget. Would you build this part as a fixed workflow or as an agent? Give your choice and two reasons that come from the facts in this case.

A student writes: "My 3D prints keep warping off the bed and I don't know why." Answering well may need several manual searches, a look at which printer the student used, and follow-up questions, and nobody can say in advance which of these will be needed or in what order. Explain why a fixed workflow is a poor fit for this request and what you would use instead (one or two sentences).

In testing, your team's booking assistant gives the model three tools (check_calendar, check_training, create_booking) and a system prompt that says "always check training before booking". About 1 request in 20, the model books first and checks training afterwards, and the number of model calls per request varies from 3 to 9. Name the root cause in terms of who controls the order of steps, and describe the design change that removes the problem (two or three sentences).

You have moved booking to a fixed workflow: check calendar, check training, create booking, always in that order. A student writes: "Book the laser cutter Friday, or if it is taken, the 3D printer instead, whichever has a slot after 2 pm." Say why the workflow cannot handle this request as built, and give one way to handle it without turning the whole booking process into an agent (two sentences).
